hook.line: "Sell me this pen" - one of the most important sales principles out there.
hook.visual: Black screen; a glowing white line-art hand rises holding a pen, then the pen sits inside a circle of $, check, cross and chart icons.

beats.what: Neon line-art hand offers a pen over the 'Sell me this pen' caption
An eye shape draws on as he promises to break it down
Checklist of ticks with one cross: it is NOT about listing features
Pen icon for the 'exotic materials' feature talk
Calendar and clock beside the pen: not about price or how long it lasts
Grid of circles with one apart: getting to know the person in front of you
Focus brackets frame one dot as the prospect's needs are identified
Pen redrawn as a rocket: the solution transforms their experience
Megaphone with social icons: put this in your own marketing

why_it_works: A famous interview line as the opener borrows recognition: viewers know the phrase but not the answer.
Every claim gets its own glowing icon that draws on, about 11 motion events a minute, so the single 70 s shot never sits still.
'What it is not' before 'what it is' builds a small reveal in the middle.
Minimal black-and-white style keeps the eye on one icon at a time.
weaknesses: Captions are tiny (median 4% of frame height) and almost all outside the safe area.
Faceless voiceover with no cuts can feel like a lecture.
No ask at the end; it closes on a vague 'keep this in mind'.
for_robert: Draw one simple line icon per claim, timed to the word that names it; Fred could hold or point at the icon. Keep captions larger than this video does.
